questions.question: What does an 'eval gate' add to a traditional CI/CD pipeline?
options: It replaces all traditional unit tests entirely
An automated check that runs a candidate change against a golden dataset and blocks deployment if output quality regresses beyond a threshold
It only checks server uptime, nothing about output quality
It is identical to a traditional unit test with no meaningful difference
questions.explanation: An eval gate specifically checks output quality against a golden dataset baseline, catching regressions that traditional code-focused tests (which only verify the code runs correctly) would miss entirely.

questions.question: Why should prompt changes go through version control and review, similar to code changes?
options: Prompts never actually affect application behavior
A prompt change can shift model behavior and introduce a quality regression just as easily as a code change, so it deserves the same reviewable, revertible, tracked process
Prompts are automatically validated by the model provider, so no review is needed
This is unnecessary since prompts are just plain text with no real impact
questions.explanation: Since prompts directly influence model behavior and output quality, treating them as unversioned, unreviewed text edits creates the same risk as making unreviewed code changes directly in production.

questions.question: A team's CI/CD pipeline passes all traditional unit tests and auto-deploys a prompt change that turns out to cause a quality regression. Which question best identifies the missing safeguard?
options: Should we just trust that passing unit tests means the change is safe?

Does our CI/CD pipeline include an eval gate comparing quality scores to a production baseline, given that traditional tests only verify the code runs correctly, not that output quality is acceptable?
Should we stop running any automated tests at all?
Is this an unavoidable risk of using AI that can't be mitigated?
questions.explanation: This scenario is the direct symptom of a missing eval gate — traditional CI/CD checks that code works, but only an eval gate specifically checks that output quality hasn't regressed, which is the safeguard that would have caught this before deployment.
